message.content: {"name":"end_turn","parameters":{"public_message":"Pinks stay up. Virginia is $500 — jail exits walk straight through that stretch.","private_thought":"No debt. Cash $86. Do not sell Virginia (3h=$500 spike → 2h=$180 for $50) unless a debt forces it; only then, to cover red 1h ($90–$100) or 3-RR ($100). Do not unmortgage CT ($66 → $20, still blocks p3 light blues). Do not trade CT, St James (orange split), PA (green lever; p4 can buy Pacific), B&O (blocks p2 4th RR), or pinks. p2 in jail can mortgage RRs and push dark blues to 3h — never pay them. p4 rich, no set, already rejected PA. Win path is jail exits hitting Virginia. End."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $86 and am on Tennessee Avenue. I own a pink monopoly with 3-2-2 houses. Virginia has 3 houses, States has 2, and St Charles has 2. Most of my other properties are mortgaged.

Opponent p2 is in jail with $195 and owns dark blues with 2 houses each. p3 has $53 and owns light blues plus reds with 1 house each. p4 has $1081, is in jail, and holds a GOOJF card without a monopoly. Atlantic, Marvin Gardens, and Pacific are unowned.

Unmortgaging Connecticut Avenue would cost $66, leaving only $20. Selling the third house on Virginia Avenue is not an option. The best path is to end the turn and wait for the pink monopoly to collect rent.

Unmortgaging Connecticut would not help me collect rent meaningfully, since its rent is low and it does not complete a set. Selling the third house on Virginia Avenue would reduce the rent from $500 to $150.

Selling the third house on Virginia Avenue would drop rent from $500 to $180. That is too large a loss to accept unless forced. I should not trade away Connecticut, St. James, Pennsylvania, or B&O. p4 has $1081 and is in jail.

p4's orange set is split three ways. The yellows and greens are also incomplete. p4 has no completed monopoly.

p2 can mortgage two railroads to raise $400. That is enough to build three houses on each dark blue property. They would then collect $1100 and $1700 per turn.

I am mapping the spaces ahead. The next reds are Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois, each with one house. I need to verify their exact rent values before deciding how to survive the trip.

The reds ahead are too expensive. Kentucky and Indiana each cost $90, and Illinois costs $100. With only $86, I would be short on every one of them. Selling the third house on Virginia Avenue would give me enough cash to cover those lands, but it would destroy the $500 rent spike. I am deciding whether to trade or sell preemptively.

I will not sell the Virginia house preemptively. The $500 rent spike is my win condition.

p2 is in jail. p3 rolled doubles and escaped from jail. p4 is still in jail after rolling a 3 and 6.

I am checking who will land on the pink properties next.

p3 has already passed the pink properties and is on St. James Place. p4 and p2 are both in jail, so they will likely land on the pinks when they exit. I am now considering trading away the B&O railroad to block p2 from completing a fourth railroad, which would raise their rent from $100 to $200.

Trading the B&O railroad to p2 would backfire by giving them a fourth railroad. Trading it to p4 or p3 would not complete any set for them. Pennsylvania Avenue does not help p4 complete greens because Pacific is still unowned, and p4 previously rejected a similar offer. St James Place cannot complete an orange set alone. Connecticut Avenue should not go to p3 because it blocks their light blue set.

I am now considering buying a red property from p3 to break their one-house monopoly. That would slash the rent on those spaces from $90 or $100 down to base rent. p4 has too much cash and no set to complete, while p3 is too poor to pay much.

Standard Monopoly rules require selling all houses on a color group before trading any property in that set. If I offer to buy a red from p3, they would need to sell their houses first. The game engine may enforce this requirement when processing the trade.

Selling three houses on a red would net p3 only $225, leaving them with $278. They would not trade away a red at that price while holding a one-house monopoly. I cannot afford to overpay for a red from them. I am now considering trading with p2.

Trading a pink property to p2 would destroy my rent income and leave me with no defense against their dark blues. I am now considering selling Pennsylvania Avenue to p4 for cash to buffer against the upcoming red rents.

I am now in the post-turn phase. The dice were rolled and movement resolved earlier, so I can only take optional actions before ending my turn.

I arrived at Tennessee Avenue, p3's mortgaged property, with no rent due. No post-turn action is required, so I will end the turn.

I considered trading St. James Place to p4 for cash. That would not complete their orange set, and the mortgaged property is worth only about $180.

St. James Place blocks both p3 and p4 from completing an orange set. Consolidating it toward the rich player would let them build hotels immediately with their $1081 cash. I will not trade away this blocker.

I will not trade St. James Place to p3 or Pennsylvania Avenue to p4, since either would let them build a green monopoly with their $1081 cash. The B&O railroad is also too valuable to give up.

No trade is clearly positive expected value. Proposing a bad offer would waste the single post-turn action.

I am now looking for a trade that could help if accepted but would be harmless if rejected. I do not have a small asset to offer p4 for cash, and I am considering asking p2 for a railroad.

I will not ask p2 for a railroad or offer p3 immunity. A trade with p4 would likely be rejected again, since they previously turned down a similar offer and are sophisticated enough to see through a misleading deal.

I am now considering buying a red property from p3 to break their one-house monopoly. That would slash rent on the upcoming pink properties. I would need to offer B&O, PA, and cash. The engine may require selling all houses first. p3 would demand compensation for that loss.

Selling a red property to p3 would destroy my own pink monopoly and leave both players without sets, letting p2 win with dark blues. Unmortgaging Connecticut Avenue would cost $66 and leave only $20 cash, which is worse than the current buffer of $86. No trade is viable, so I will end the turn.
